page.layout: One printed page of running text, with small notes in the left margin. The strip at the right edge is the neighbouring page and is left out. Reading order: the running head, then the text column top to bottom, the notes in the left margin beside their lines, then the catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: vito, aliquid contra Leges attentare: fieri enim illud licere debitis conditionibus observatis; hoc nullâ conditione licere. Dico secundò, Subditi si quid attentare velint in ordine ad salutem publicam, duas præ cæteris conditiones sanctissimæ esse observandas: quarum alterutram qui neglexerint, nullâ necessitatis excusatione se tueri posse. Eas quàm sanctè observarint, qui funestissimorum in hoc regno motuum vel Authores extiterunt vel Fautores, dicere non est meum: ipsi viderint. Sunt autem duæ illæ conditiones, istæ: Altera, ut quid fiat, tentetúrve fieri in Principis præjudicium, cujus persona & dignitas interest salutis publicæ, ut sartæ tectæ conserventur. Altera, ne quid militer fiat, fierive tentetur contra Leges & jura, nisi ex Principis consensu; consensu nempe, vel expresso, ubi commodè haberi potest, vel (ubi longius abest, nec res patitur moram,) rationabiliter saltem præsumpto. Tunc autem abesse Principis consensus rationabiliter præsumitur; cùm tam magna tamque {1}evidensIn manifestis non opus est interpretatione, sed executione. premit necessitas, ut nemo sanus & prudens possit dubitare, Principem ipsum, si ibi tum præsens esset, Legis gratiam & relaxationem subditis concessurum.

XXI. Duabus hisce conditionibus observatis, nihil aliunde aboriatur (ex particularibus scil. circumstantiis,) impedimentum, Aquin. 2. 2. q. 120. art. 10.{2}licere dico subditis pro tuendâ adversus externos hostes vel domesticos perduelles, Principis & Populi salute, ad communem utilitatem spectare magis, quæ Suprema Lex est, quàm ad voces & apices Legum particularium; quæ propterea latæ sunt, ut communi utilitati inserviant, non præjudicent. Ratio manifesta est: quia media sunt propter finem, non finis propter media: & proinde media fini inservire debent, non finis inservire mediis. Quum ergo salus publica habeat rationem Finis, Leges autem
{2} Certum est omnia licere propatria. Quintil. declamat. 369.

page.notes: The notes in the left margin are set in small italic type. Their reference marks are read from the superscripts in the text. The mark for the second note is doubtful, and the note reads "a Certum est" in print, so it is placed as the second mark. The bare reference "Aquin." is printed with its line broken, and "A qu n." was read as "Aquin.". Words in the running text are doubtful where the scan is faint, notably "tentetúrve", "militer" and "aboriatur". The strip at the right edge belongs to the neighbouring page and is left out. "Leges autem" ends the page; the catchword is read from the right margin.
